text:
It's Sept. 1. Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong is telling us to wake him up when September ends.

Filipinos, meanwhile, are already waking up to Jose Mari Chan peeping on their news feeds. And somewhere in the background, Mariah Carey is probably singing, “I don't want a lot for Christmas…”

The “Ber” months are officially here, and with them, what Filipinos consider the world's longest Christmas season. For decades, Sept. 1 has meant the return of Christmas memes, playlists, countdowns and sales.

But why do we start so early?

COUNTDOWN CULTURE

Sociologist Bro. Clifford Sorita offered four reasons in a 2020 LinkedIn post.

First, it helps us anticipate a horizon. Sorita wrote that “time moves according to how we anticipate horizons.” For Filipinos, Christmas becomes that horizon—a hopeful event ahead that gives us something to look forward to and, as he puts it, makes the remaining days of the year more bearable.

It also creates a sense of urgency. Sorita noted that starting early gives us time to “plan, prepare and prioritize," instead of cramming gifts, travel and reunions into the Christmas rush. Four months suddenly doesn't seem so excessive.

That head start, Sorita said, can also help calm our Christmas anxieties. The holidays come with expectations of happy, seamless and picture-perfect celebrations, which can also bring stress and disappointment. Celebrating early, he said, gives us more time to prepare and manage those expectations.

And ultimately, it gives us more time for the essential things before Christmas. For Sorita, those essentials are “faith, family and friends.” For Filipinos separated from loved ones by work or distance, the long season gives them more time to save, book a flight and make plans to be together—in his words, “Being Home for Christmas.”

FILIPINIZATION OF CHRISTMAS

Christmas came with Christianity, but Filipinos turned it into something distinctly their own. In "Christmas in the Philippines: Beyond Popular Religious Tradition"—published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Multidisciplinary Research in 2020—Rev. Fr. Antonio Noel Carbayas and theologian Fides del Castillo described how the celebration has become woven into Filipino family and social life.

They pointed out how Christmas has been “Filipinized”—a blend of faith and local traditions, from Simbang Gabi and the belen to family reunions, gift-giving, food, and homecomings. Commercialism, they noted, has also made the season more festive and extravagant.

But beneath the noise and spending is something more enduring: connection. Grandparents wait for grandchildren. Friends organize reunions. Families separated by work or migration make plans to come together.

For Filipinos, especially those working overseas, Christmas isn't just a religious celebration. It's also a reason to come home.

OLDER STORY ABOUT SEPTEMBER

Filipino-American historian and content creator Kirby Araullo offers a different take: September may have been culturally significant long before Christmas arrived.

In a September 2025 YouTube video, Araullo argued that “our September celebrations have a much deeper environmental foundation than most people realize.”

For agricultural communities, he said, the month marked a critical seasonal transition that could mean the difference between “survival and abundance.” Its timing, he added, came from reading “natural signs from Mother Nature,” rather than simply following a fixed calendar.

That doesn't mean precolonial Filipinos celebrated Christmas in September. Araullo's point is that the season itself may have already carried meaning before Christianity gave it a new one.

So here we are again: Sept. 1, Jose Mari Chan on the feed, Mariah Carey in the background, and four months of Christmas ahead.

text:
Good morning, dear friends. As the first light of September 1, 2026, gently fills the sky, I hope this message finds you with a warm cup in hand and a quiet moment to reflect. The verse for today, drawn from 1 Peter 3:6, offers a simple yet powerful promise: "...I will not be afraid..." It invites us to live with courage even when everyday pressures feel heavy.

Many of us wake to news of shifting job markets and rising costs that stir worry about the months ahead. Families navigate health concerns or the quiet ache of distance from loved ones, while communities face ongoing questions about stability and the environment. These real-life challenges can make fear feel like a constant companion, whispering doubts about what tomorrow holds.

Yet the words of Scripture gently redirect our gaze. They remind us that we do not face these moments alone. Just as Sarah trusted in God's care amid uncertainty, we too can choose to move forward with hope. This morning, take a breath and notice the small mercies around you: the sound of birds, a text from a friend, or the simple gift of another day.

In 2026, we see both struggle and progress—people coming together in local efforts, new technologies bringing comfort, and faith communities offering steady support. Letting go of fear does not mean ignoring problems; it means facing them with a heart anchored in trust. Carry that quiet strength into your meetings, errands, or conversations today.

May this verse settle like sunlight in your spirit, bringing peace that lasts beyond the morning hours. You are held, you are loved, and you need not be afraid.

Many of you who say you serve Me, are not fit to stand up and declare yourself to be a servant of God 

Saturday, August 31st, 2013 @ 21:45

My dearly beloved daughter, I told you all some time ago, to plant seeds in order to feed you and your families, during the persecution. I do this for a reason. You must plant, even just a few seeds – pure seeds, which have not been tampered with by human interference. I will then multiply the fruit which they will yield and all will have enough to eat when the world will experience great hunger. Those days are not far away and they will come about for a number of reasons.

The crops will be contaminated through the intervention of greedy farmers. The result crops will be unfit for you to eat. Then war will mean that few men will be able to till the land. Then there will be the fire, which will pour over the four corners of the earth, and everything will become barren. These terrible trials will be caused by the spread of evil, but many people will survive if they trust in Me. You must prepare now, as if a war is coming and as you would when food is rationed. Have plenty of water because everything you store will be multiplied by Me.

Please do not believe that I ask you to leave your homes for this is not necessary. A little preparation, where you offer help to each other, is all that is needed. My Precious Blood will cover all those who believe in My Warning to humanity for the time of the Third Seal to open will follow a time of war.

So many will ignore the Word of God, which is contained in the Book of Revelation. So many leaders and sacred servants in My churches, fail to respond to My prophet, just as they did before the flood.

I call to My sacred servants now. Who do you believe in? Me, your Jesus or the ramblings of those who claim to be experts in theology, but who are ignorant of the Truth? Wake up. The Seals have opened. Your duty is to help Me to save souls, but you have not remained alert to the sound of My Call. I have told you that I will come like a thief in the night. When that day comes it will be too late for souls who have not prepared.

The time for the trumpets to peel out their judgements will come quickly, no sooner than when the Seals have been laid bare. What then? Will you wake up and follow Me at that stage or will you lose Me more souls, while you hesitate? While you wait for others to lead the way?

I must remind you that your role is to save souls. You do this through a life where you are supposed to serve Me and not where you pander to the pride and ego of those who try to twist My Teachings. Many of you in My churches do not understand the meaning of My New Paradise and have failed to remind God’s children of My Promise. You must remind them of the Truth – of the time, before the final day.

text:
The Indian opposition is going to have a fun time for a while in the wake of the Delhi demonstrations.  

They will offer themselves as the alternative to the BJP, promising lots of good white collar jobs which Modi has failed to provide.

Maybe they will get power at the centre and in the states.

Then they will find themselves stuck.    How to deliver the promised jobs?   

India's Nehruite economy is extremely hard to change fundamentally.   

Indian factories cannot expand fast because bigger factories cannot lay off workers or hire them easily due to tough labour rules imposed by Nehru.   Unions will defend those rules ruthlessly.  Rahul Gandhi can do nothing about that.  His party opposes a more flexible labour code.

Indian workers are perpetually on strike, deterring domestic and foreign investment.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.

Land for factories and infrastructure is hard to buy in India because too much compensation is demanded and there are endless court battles.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.   In fact his party helped stop BJP led attempts to make land purchases for industry easier.

High protectionism imposed by Nehru means Indian firms lack the incentive to produce goods of quality good enough to sell in the world market.  So India is poor at exporting goods.  The system benefits Indian industrialists who fund political parties.  Rahul Gandhi cannot change that.

More good jobs in education and health care needs a lot more government spending on both areas.  But India cannot tax rich farmers and so governments do not have the money for such spending.  Nehru perpetuated the no tax of rich farmers policy.  No government dares to abolish it.  Rahul Gandhi can do nothing about it.

So what can Rahul Gandhi offer?

Caste quotas in jobs and education.  This is the opposite of what the upper caste students who are protesting want.

Heigh ho!   

Modi has no answers.    He is on a sticky wicket.

But so is Rahul Gandhi and the opposition.

If they win there will be short term euphoria and then complete disillusionment. 

The cocky Cockroach Party is doomed to disappointment.

No government and no party has easy answers for India.

How strange that no-one in the Indian and foreign press is pointing out these obvious facts!

text:
I had $22,000 in debt and no degree at 18. By 21 I was making $50,000 a month

Not crypto. Not dropshipping. Not inherited money.

Day trading on prop firm accounts. Using one strategy I learned for free on YouTube.

Everyone told me to be realistic. Here's what "realistic" looks like:

Realistic path I was told to follow:
- Take out $80k in student loans
- Get a business degree in 4 years
- Apply for jobs. Get rejected. Apply again
- Land a $45k/year entry position at 23
- Spend 15 years paying off combined $102k in debt
- Maybe make $80k/year by 35 if I'm lucky

What I actually did (after 3 years of wasting my time):

Month 1-3: Watched YouTube every free moment I had. Learned one price action strategy. Practiced it on a free demo account while delivering food 10 hours a day. I'd park between deliveries and pull up TradingView on my phone. Mark my levels. Review my trades from that morning. Study, deliver, study, deliver

Month 4-5: Started demo trading the London session (2-5am EST) because my morning delivery job shift blocked the New York session. Woke up at 1:45am every day. Sat in bed with my laptop. Traded until 4:30am. Slept until 7. Delivered food from 8am-6pm. Studied charts from 7pm-10pm. Slept 4-5 hours a night for 3 months straight

Month 6: Bought first prop firm challenge. $100. Failed on day 17 because I broke my max drawdown rule. I got emotional after two consecutive losses and took a revenge trade with double my normal position size. Classic beginner mistake. That one trade cost me the entire challenge

Month 7: Bought second challenge. $100. This time I wrote my rules on a sticky note and put it on my monitor: "1% risk maximum. 2 trades maximum per day. No trading after a loss." Passed in 22 days with 6% profit. Got a $100k funded account

Month 7-10: Passed 4 more challenges while still delivering food. Now trading $500k+ in funded capital. My morning routine: wake up at 1:45am, trade London session, take 1-2 trades, close laptop by 4:30am, sleep until 7, deliver food all day

Month 12: First $20k month. Quit the delivery job. The math made it pointless. One winning trade was worth more than an entire day of deliveries. I was delivering burritos for $150/day while making $3,000 from a single trade I took at 3am. At some point it's just insulting to yourself to keep doing both

Month 12+: Hit $50k/month across all of my funded accounts. Paid off all $22,000 in debt in one transfer. Walked into the bank and wired the full amount. The teller asked what I did for a living. I said "I stare at candles." She looked at me like I was insane

Here's what nobody tells you about the actual journey though:

The first 3 months are brutal. You're learning something completely new. You're bad at it. Every day you look at your journal and see more red than green. You question whether you're wasting your time. Your friends think you've lost your mind. Your family keeps asking when you're going to "do something real"

You'll want to switch strategies around week 6. Don't. The strategy isn't broken. You are. And the only way to fix yourself is repetition. Stay on the same setup. Keep journaling. The breakthrough always comes after the point where most people quit

The lonely nights are real. Trading the London session means you're awake when everyone's asleep. 3am. Just you, a laptop, and a chart. No one to talk to. No one who understands what you're doing. You'll sit there watching a candle form for 15 minutes wondering if this is all worth it

It is. But you won't believe that until the first time you see $5,000 hit your account from a trade you took in your underwear at 3:17am while everyone you know was sleeping

That moment changes something inside you permanently. You can never go back to thinking like an employee after that. The cage door is open and you can see outside

Total cost of my "education": $0 (YouTube)
Total cost to access $500k+ in capital: roughly $1,500 in challenge fees
Time invested: 6 months of learning + practice before seeing real money

People told me trading was a scam. That it was gambling. That I needed to "grow up and get a real job"

Those same people are now asking me how I did it

This August 31, join Bishop Konderla for "Called by Name", a seven-day prayer journey on the Hallow app. Whether you are discerning God's direction for your life or simply seeking to grow closer to Him, these daily reflections offer an opportunity to listen more attentively to His voice.

Throughout the week, you'll hear stories of ordinary men and women who discovered God's call in unexpected ways. Together, we'll reflect on the beauty of the many vocations through which God leads His people to holiness, including marriage, the priesthood, religious life, the diaconate, and consecrated single life.

As the journey concludes, Bishop will share a little of his own vocation story and invite all of us to pray for those who are discerning where the Lord is calling us. Our encouragement, prayers, and witness can make a lasting difference in helping someone respond with courage and trust.

...because they decided it was "NOT MEDICALLY NECESSARY" even though his doctor's said it was!!!

His name is Peyton Alvarez, he's 25 years old.

Back in April, Peyton was riding his motorcycle near Greenville, South Carolina, when he veered off the road and hit a tree.

He was wearing his helmet, but. the impact left him with a traumatic brain injury so severe that doctors call his condition a "disorder of consciousness."

His mother Trina got the call every parent on earth prays they never get. "We have your son Peyton, and he's been in a motorcycle accident."

There is a place that specializes in bringing people like Peyton back. The Shepherd Center in Atlanta, one of the best brain injury rehab centers in the country.

And it wasn't just his family who wanted him there. His DOCTORS recommended it.

The people who actually examined Peyton said this is the care he needs to recover.

And UnitedHealthcare said NO.

Their reason, in writing:

Peyton's condition "does not meet the criteria" for the rehab his family requested.

In plain English? They called the treatment that could help this young man wake up "not medically necessary."

Not one person at that insurance company has ever laid eyes on Peyton. His doctors have, but UnitedHealthcare overrode them anyway.

Instead, they offered a NURSING HOME.

Yes, you read that right... a nursing home.

Consumption is splitting further along income lines. Richmond offered a nuanced twist: even affluent clients at a luxury salon spent more on injectable treatments but stretched out haircut intervals and skipped add-on services, suggesting selective cutbacks even among higher earners. Kansas City bankers flagged a credit-quality wrinkle: roughly half of new auto loans involve negative equity from trade-ins, an early sign of household financial stress building beneath the surface. It portrays someone

moving for work

and contract assignments
 across many states—
yet still treats 
the connections formed along the way a
s real and worth mourning. 

The tone is neither dramatic

about impermanence
 and quietly hopeful 
about what might come after. 

He values the people 
more than the place

the character of his circle.

Bonnie Brown
 replies with her own story

 Other friends

who crossed paths with him
 in different seasons 
and still check in. 

They treat the move 
as both an ending 
and a continuation, 
which matches how he frames it.

Taken together,
the post and replies

who has lived
 a geographically scattered professional life,

f geographically scattered friends,

 at this stage,

in relationships

states that came and went

Managed Money Positions Overview
September 2, 2026

Data Period: Positions as of August 25, 2026 (NA) | August 28, 2026 (EU)

Market Sentiment & Technical Narrative

A historic wave of speculative capital has reshaped the agricultural sector, culminating in one of the fastest managed money net buying surges on record. Driven by persistent late August crop degradation across the western Corn Belt and expanding logistical constraints in the Black Sea, funds added over 500,000 net contracts across major grains and softs in late August. This buying frenzy pushed managed money’s net long exposure in corn and soybeans to multi-year highs, aggressively pricing in a tighter supply balance ahead of early harvest results.

In stark contrast to the row crop rally, the livestock sector is suffering from a systematic unwinding of long risk. A confluence of record low packer margins, dropping boxed beef values, and expanding processing delays has triggered sustained liquidations in live cattle. While the official reopening of southern entry points to Mexican feeder imports continues to slowly rebuild calf pipelines, lean hog spec length has collapsed to near year low levels under seasonal carcass pressure.

Top News Story: Record Ag Buying Pace & Late-Pod Soybean Drop

The central market driver entering September is the unprecedented velocity of speculative accumulation alongside late season crop stress. The USDA’s August 31 Crop Progress update confirmed that national corn condition ratings held at a season low 57% good to excellent (12 percentage points below last year’s 69%), with 92% in dough, 62% dented, and 13% mature. 

Soybean ratings deteriorated further to 58% good to excellent (down 2 percentage points) as late pod set and seed fill phases encountered late August heat and moisture deficits across the central and southern Plains.

On the policy and trade front, commodity markets are adjusting to broader hard asset capital flows following US Treasury policy shifts and renewed shipping risk in the Middle East and Black Sea. In protein logistics, western feedlots continue to monitor cross-border movement following the August 24 reopening of the Douglas, Arizona port of entry for Mexican live cattle, keeping feeder calf supply channels on a gradual recovery path.

Soybean Meal, CBOT: +96,000 | +12,600 | 422,100 | Stable

Technical Spotlights:
Corn Funds Blast Off: Managed money bought a massive 135,756 net-long contracts in a single week the sharpest single week accumulation in 24 weeks lifting their net long to +317,448 contracts (98th percentile of the 52-week range). December futures firmed past $5.10/bu as spec length aligned with seasonal yield concerns.

Soybean Longs Top 200k: Speculators expanded their net long stance by 48,897 contracts to reach +200,679 contracts, propelled by a 2 point drop in national soybean conditions down to 58% and firming September futures near $12.76/bu.

Wheat Shorts Squeezed Further: Chicago SRW wheat funds trimmed their net short position down to -13,597 contracts (up 11,731 on the week), while Kansas City HRW wheat funds expanded length to a four-year high of +42,514 net long contracts.

EU Insight
European milling wheat on the MATIF exchange continues to hold firm technical support. Driven by shrinking EU+UK production estimates and a sharp reduction in regional ending stocks, European fund managers are maintaining flat to mildly long positions. 

The upside remains monitored as Black Sea cash offers continue to compete aggressively for Middle Eastern export tenders despite mounting shipping insurance premiums.

North American Livestock Exchanges
(Managed Money Net | Funds Δ | Open Interest | OI Δ)

Feeder Cattle, CME: +8,900 | -1,400 | 51,400 | Stable

Lean Hogs, CME: -36,100 | -7,100 | 258,900 | Stable

Livestock Sector Deep Dive:
Cattle Position Erosion: Live cattle speculative net length slid to +59,700 contracts, reaching the 0th percentile of its 52 week range as October live cattle futures dropped toward $211.72/cwt. Packer margins remaining deeply in the red continue to cap cash cattle bids.

Feeder Calf Range: Feeder cattle funds trimmed positions down to +8,900 contracts, with September futures settling near $320.90/cwt. Elevated grain input prices and expanding border imports are keeping feeder lot buying conservative.

Hog Short Expansion: Lean hog funds expanded net-short exposure by 7,100 contracts to settle at -36,100 net short contracts, as October hog futures slid toward $81.90/cwt under seasonal carcass supply increases.

The Week Ahead: Critical Drivers
Combine Yield Verification: As early harvest expands beyond the Delta and southern Corn Belt, early yield reports will test whether field results match the USDA's lowered 180.7 bu/acre corn baseline.

Pre-September WASDE Positioning: Traders will begin positioning ahead of the September 11 USDA WASDE report, looking for objective field updates on soybean pod counts and regional corn test weights.

Black Sea Freight Rates: Monitor escalation in maritime shipping lanes and fuel surcharges, which are directly impacting transatlantic grain arbitrage and destination cash bids.

text:
On this date in 1951 English Violinist, Violaist, Keyboardist, and former member of ELO, Michael Kaminski is born in Harrogate, England.

Kaminski applied for the vacant spot as ELO's violinist because of an advertisement in Melody Maker. He was recruited after 2 interviews and was also the only person auditioning who did not play a wrong note. Jeff Lynne held the audition. Kaminski 1st appeared on ELO's 1973 studio album On the Third Day, playing violin on 4 tracks.

During his stint in ELO, Kaminski initially tried to imitate his predecessor Wilf Gibson by wearing a cape while playing the violin, but soon acquired his trademark blue violin, which he has played variants of ever since. Kaminski's own band is called Blue Violin.

Kaminski was one of the 3 remaining string players for the group when Lynne decided to remove them in 1980, although Kaminski had not appeared on any of the band's studio recordings since 77's Out of the Blue by the time of his dismissal. Unlike fellow string players Hugh McDowell and Melvyn Gale, however, Kaminski returned to perform on the tours for the ELO albums Time and Balance of Power, and on the '83 single "Rock 'n' Roll Is King". Kaminski likewise appeared prominently on ELO bandmember Kelly Groucutt's '82 solo album. Following ELO's breakup in 1986, Kaminski formed the group Player alongside Groucutt; the pair were joined by former ELO cellist Hugh McDowell several years later. Increasingly dissatisfied with the promotional campaign for OrKestra, Kaminski, Groucutt and McDowell accepted an offer to perform in the debut tour for the ELO spinoff band ELO Part II in 1991. While promoted as guest artists from OrKestra, Kaminski, Groucutt and McDowell performed alongside Part II as a single 8 piece unit during the tour. By 1993, Kaminski and Groucutt dissolved OrKestra and became full time members of Part II; Kaminski thereby prominently features on the group's 2nd album Moment of Truth, both playing violin on and receiving songwriting credits for several tracks. Kaminski continued to perform with ELO Part II for the remainder of its lifetime.

Upon ELO Part II's rebranding as The Orchestra in 2000, Kaminski chose to remain with the band, contributing violin parts to its sole released studio album No Rewind the following year. Following Louis Clark's death in 2021, Kaminski became the sole member of the Orchestra to have formerly been a member or affiliate of the original ELO, holding the title until his retirement in January 2026.

Apart from the hits he had with ELO, in early 1979 Kaminski made the Top 40 of the UK Singles Chart as the frontman of a one hit wonder group called Violinski, with the single "Clog Dance". Kaminski sporadically performed "Clog Dance" live with The Orchestra.

Kaminski was featured as violinist on a selection of tracks from the second studio album, Beauty In Chaos, by the Anglo-Irish acoustic duo Fay & Latta.

text:
In the late 1960s, before fame, awards, and Hollywood success, Danny DeVito and Michael Douglas were simply two young actors chasing the same dream.

They shared a small apartment on West 89th Street in Manhattan, splitting rent, sharing meals, and stretching every dollar they could. The apartment wasn't much to look at—cramped rooms, scattered scripts, empty coffee cups, and the constant uncertainty that comes with trying to break into a difficult profession.

The two first met in 1967 at the Eugene O'Neill Theater Center in Connecticut. Michael was attending a summer acting workshop, while Danny was working there. They connected almost immediately through their humor, ambition, and love of storytelling.

When both eventually moved to New York to pursue acting careers, becoming roommates seemed like the natural choice.

Life for aspiring actors was far from glamorous. Days were spent racing between auditions, waiting for callbacks that often never came, and dealing with rejection after rejection. During those difficult moments, they became each other's support system.

Whenever one returned home discouraged, the other was there to lift his spirits, offer advice, or simply provide a laugh when it was needed most.

Although their personalities were different, they complemented one another perfectly. Danny's energy, humor, and warmth balanced Michael's focused, thoughtful, and determined nature. Together, they spent countless evenings rehearsing scenes, discussing characters, and helping each other improve their craft.

They weren't just roommates—they were friends, critics, collaborators, and believers in each other's potential.

Years later, Michael Douglas fondly reflected on those early days, remembering Danny as someone who could brighten any room and keep people's spirits high no matter how difficult life became.

Danny spoke just as warmly about Michael, describing him as hardworking, grounded, and like a brother during a period when neither of them had much money but both had enormous dreams.

Eventually, the years of persistence paid off.

When Michael produced One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, he made sure Danny was part of the cast, helping introduce him to a wider audience. Their friendship later translated effortlessly to the screen in films such as Romancing the Stone, The Jewel of the Nile, and The War of the Roses.

The chemistry audiences saw wasn't acting—it was built on years of trust, shared struggles, and genuine friendship.

Decades later, despite the demands of family life, career successes, personal setbacks, and health challenges, their bond remains intact.

What began as two struggling actors sharing a tiny New York apartment became one of Hollywood's most enduring friendships.

Their story is a reminder that success may change many things, but the friendships formed before the spotlight often become the most valuable of all.

From broke dreamers to cinema legends, Danny DeVito and Michael Douglas prove that true friendship isn't measured by fame or fortune—it's measured by loyalty, support, and the people who stood beside you long before the world knew your name.

Yes, Azerbaijan announced that Armenians could “stay” if they accepted Azerbaijani citizenship and jurisdiction. That does not rebut ethnic cleansing.

Ethnic cleansing does not require a formal deportation order. It includes creating conditions of force, intimidation, fear, and coercion that make continued residence impossible.

And Azerbaijan’s intent cannot be divorced from the rhetoric of its own president. During the 2020 war, Ilham Aliyev repeatedly dehumanized Armenians, describing them as “mice,” “dogs,” “wild beasts,” “predators” and “jackals” and portraying them in explicitly vermin-like terms while promising to drive them out. Azerbaijan then issued the notorious 2020 stamp imagery showing Nagorno-Karabakh being fumigated by an exterminator, visually presenting Armenians as something to be disinfected or eradicated.

Then came the blockade, the humanitarian crisis, the September 2023 military assault, and the flight of more than 100,000 Armenians, virtually the entire indigenous Armenian population of Nagorno-Karabakh in a matter of days.

So spare me the “but they offered citizenship” defense. A state does not get to dehumanize a population as vermin, blockade it, attack it, terrify it into flight, and then point to an offer of citizenship as proof that nobody was forced out.

And your source dodge changes nothing. Remove Freedom House and HRW entirely. You still have the International Court of Justice ordering Azerbaijan to ensure the safe return of Armenians and protect them from force or intimidation causing them to flee, and the Council of Europe concluding that Armenians fled amid a genuine threat to their physical security.

“We told them they could stay after making them afraid to stay” is not a defense to ethnic cleansing.

And “Azerbaijanis were expelled in the 1990s, therefore Armenians may be expelled now” is even worse. That is not an argument against ethnic cleansing. It is an argument for retaliatory ethnic cleansing.

text:
Over the years God has moved me to write down my own questions and His answers as a way of collecting and preserving the thoughts. I've found an occasional rereading beneficial. Here's something from a few years ago - maybe someone else will find some of it useful.
------------------

I’ve found myself thinking/meditating on two of God’s self-described attributes: holiness and goodness.  I think the general understanding within the church on the concept of God’s holiness is fuzzy, and I’ve been seeking a better, deeper grasp on what holiness truly is.  I can’t say that I’ve specifically thought that much before about His “goodness” – I guess that seemed kind of obvious.  Lately, however, I see that my grasp on goodness has also been shallow (no surprise), so I’ve been trying to go deeper there as well.  In addition to being high level attributes of God in and of themselves, holiness and goodness can also be thought of as adjectives/modifiers for all of His other attributes.  I think it’s fair to say that they work on each other, too – i.e., God’s holiness is good, and His goodness is holy.
Holiness:
God tells us He is holy, but what exactly does He mean by that?  As I observe how many around me use the word “holy,” it seems that many people think the word means things like moral purity, right behavior, goodness, etc.  However, the word itself fundamentally means “separate” or “set apart.”  When God tells us He is holy He is saying that in His essence He is apart from His creation, that He is above it, outside it, not of the same substance.  When we experience things in creation that reflect on who God is, we should remember that they are indeed reflections, images – they point to the “real thing,” but they are not the real thing.  They cannot be, for He is holy.
All of God’s character attributes are holy – they are expressly not worldly.  His power is holy, His wisdom is holy, His righteousness is holy, His mercy is holy, His faithfulness is holy, etc.  As He tells us in Isaiah 55, His ways and thoughts are not our ways and thoughts, and His ways and thoughts are higher than our ways and thoughts as the heavens are higher than the earth.  He has holy thoughts and ways; we don’t.  Humans can attempt to imitate these attributes, but in and of ourselves, they will never be holy in us; we are of the world.
God’s commands us to be “holy” – behavior is involved, but I’ve come to see that these commands aren’t primarily aimed at our behavior.  They are aimed at our hearts, and He gives all of us the opportunity to see that, in and of ourselves, we cannot be holy, we can never be separate from the world, we’re part of the world.  God then offers to make it possible through spiritual rebirth for us to actually become holy.  His commands to us to be holy, rather than being demands on our behavior, are really heart-felt invitations to fellowship with Him.  He says “I’m over here, apart from the world system, holy; come over here, be holy, too, be with Me.”  He doesn’t want something from us – He wants something for us!  He wants us to choose Life Himself – that destiny we were created for.
Goodness:
God tells us in His word that He is good, but what exactly does He mean by that?  In keeping with the preceding thoughts on holiness, first I’ll remark that God’s goodness is holy – His goodness is something intrinsic to Him and apart from His creation.  Of course, His goodness permeates His creation, but it is not of His creation.  We as His creations can appreciate His goodness, but we cannot totally grasp it – again, His goodness is holy.
Goodness is a state in which everything is as it should be – it is complete, just right, perfect.  In addition to being holy, all of God’s character attributes are good, they are just right.  His power is good, His wisdom is good, His righteousness is good, His justice is good, His mercy is good, His faithfulness is good, etc. – meaning each of these attributes are exactly right and perfect.  We, as His creatures, are designed to recognize good things the way God made them, since He made them to show us things about Himself.  When we see or experience things that are “good,” they are naturally known to us as good; they need no explanation.  When we see things that are not good, likewise we need no explanation.  {I’ll interject here that there is no such thing as objective “bad.”  Bad is what happens/is in the absence of good, just as dark is what happens/is in the absence of light.}
God’s Word clearly and repeatedly states that no man is good, and it clearly states that the God is good.  Jesus questioned a man once who had called Him “good Teacher,” saying “why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.” (Mark 10:18)  {there’s a clue here that since Jesus IS good, He is God).  So how should mankind view things in our earthly experience that seem to clearly not be “good,” such as crime, cruelty, sickness, natural disasters, etc.  I can think of three general viewpoints, two of which are in error:
· Viewpoint 1: God is actually not good, since all of these “bad” things are within His control, yet He allows them anyway
· Viewpoint 2: God is good, but He is not actually sovereign; i.e., He is not strong enough or wise enough to prevent such things.  By the way, this viewpoint of God is actually inconsistent with the meaning of good, which by definition means things are complete, just right, perfect.  If such earthly things are beyond God’s control, then his strength/wisdom, etc. are not good – they are lacking, they fall short
· Viewpoint 3: The Biblical view is that “bad” things we see or experience in our temporal existence are indeed consistent with God’s goodness when seen from an eternal perspective.
I wholeheartedly subscribe to the third view.  God’s plans for man have always involved eternity.  They have never been limited to the current creation, bound by human concepts of time.  His goal is the eternal redemption of mankind via His own grace, justice, and mercy.  How He goes about accomplishing this goal is not something any of us can understand.  The best we can hope for is a type of spiritual discernment and a measure of simple faith that He knows what He is doing.  I by no means understand it all; I’m not sure I actually “understand” any of it.  What I do know and can testify to, is that God has patiently labored with me all of my days, and what He is doing for and in me is truly good.  I cannot walk in the steps of other people, but since God is no respecter of persons, I find it easy to believe that He also willingly works good in the lives of others, over and above their earthly circumstances.

This declaration sets the stage for Farley's examination of how God’s voice will once again intervene in human history at the Rapture, drawing His followers out of a world rife with turmoil.

GOLD AND SILVER ARE LEGAL TENDER IN TEXAS AS OF SEPTEMBER 1, AND NOBODY IS REQUIRED TO TAKE THEM

WHAT ACTUALLY TOOK EFFECT

· Gold and silver specie stamped with its weight and purity is now legal tender in Texas, and the provision is written for privately produced metal, since any marking suggesting a government minted or issued the piece disqualifies it.

· No person, business, or agency can be compelled to offer or accept specie for a debt, a deposit, or any other purpose, and Federal Reserve notes remain fully available for paying any debt.

· The spending mechanism is not live, because the comptroller's authority to establish or authorize electronic payment systems backed by bullion in the Texas Bullion Depository does not begin until May 1, 2027.

Legal tender status without an acceptance mandate is a definitional change before it is a monetary one, and until the payment rail exists the only way to settle in metal is a hand to hand deal between two willing parties. The date that carries weight is May 1, 2027, when Texas decides whether the depository becomes payments infrastructure or stays a vault with a statute attached.

Which arrives first in Texas, a merchant quoting prices in ounces or a state card that spends them?

Embracing Humble Growth Through 1 Corinthians 3

In the reading from 1 Corinthians 3 we encounter words that gently guide the faithful toward greater spiritual awareness and unity. Paul speaks directly to early believers who struggled with immaturity and conflict yet his message remains relevant for those seeking to deepen their relationship with God. By focusing on humility and shared purpose Catholics can find encouragement to move forward even when progress feels slow. This passage reminds readers that growth comes through reliance on divine grace rather than personal striving alone. Many who strive for holiness appreciate how these verses highlight patience with oneself and others along the way.

What Insights Does Paul Offer on Spiritual Nourishment?

The opening section of the passage addresses the distinction between spiritual maturity and fleshly inclinations in a way that invites self-reflection without condemnation. Paul states "And so brothers and sisters I could not speak to you as spiritual people but rather as people of the flesh as infants in Christ." This image of infants receiving milk rather than solid food underscores the gradual nature of faith development. Readers who sometimes fall short in their efforts can see this as an invitation to continue receiving guidance suited to their current stage. The text continues "I fed you with milk not solid food for you were not ready for solid food. Even now you are still not ready for you are still of the flesh." Such language emphasizes that readiness develops over time through consistent openness to transformation. By recognizing these stages Catholics gain hope that their sincere attempts at holiness contribute to ongoing progress even amid setbacks.

In What Ways Can We Overcome Divisions in Our Communities?

Paul then turns to the practical effects of remaining in a state of spiritual infancy noting how jealousy and quarreling reveal human limitations. He asks "For as long as there is jealousy and quarreling among you are you not of the flesh and behaving according to human inclinations?" This question points to the reality that personal ambitions can disrupt communal harmony yet it also opens the door to choosing reconciliation instead. The following verse illustrates the issue with "For when one says I belong to Paul and another I belong to Apollos are you not merely human?" Faithful individuals who aim to live charitably may relate to moments when preferences create unnecessary friction. Through this analysis the reading encourages a shift toward viewing others as fellow travelers rather than competitors. Such an approach supports daily choices that reduce sin by fostering understanding and mutual support in parishes and families alike.

How Does Acknowledging God as the Giver of Growth Transform Our Efforts?

The middle portion of the reading shifts attention to the roles of human servants in God's plan highlighting humility as a path to freedom from pride. Paul writes "What then is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you came to believe as the Lord assigned to each." This framing places human contributions in proper perspective reducing the temptation to claim sole credit for spiritual successes. He adds "I planted Apollos watered but God gave the growth." Those working to avoid sin find reassurance here that their labors matter yet ultimate results rest with divine action. The passage affirms "So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything but only God who gives the growth." This truth uplifts readers by lightening the burden of perfection and inviting trust in a power greater than individual willpower. In daily life this perspective helps maintain peace when outcomes differ from expectations.

What Does It Mean to Be Co-Workers in God's Field Today?

The final verses emphasize collaboration and shared purpose among believers as they participate in God's work. Paul explains "The one who plants and the one who waters have a common purpose and each will receive wages according to the labor of each." This statement rewards consistent effort while affirming that all contributions hold value in the larger picture. He concludes the section with "For we are God's servants working together you are God's field God's building." Such imagery portrays the community as a living space tended by many hands under one divine architect. Catholics striving for holiness discover in these words motivation to support one another rather than compete. The overall message promotes a lifestyle where humility and cooperation naturally steer one away from divisive behaviors toward a more integrated and peaceful existence.

May the peace of Christ be with you,

text: I'm a small business owner in Oregon who employs 25 employees.   I was born on the south coast, fishing, hunting, clamming, crabbing and mushroom hunting.  Basically enjoying everything that Oregon had to offer a small coastal town.  I went to Oregon public schools, and moved on to graduate from Oregon State University.  I had a great life growing up and  Oregon's geography is amazing. I've had a thriving business in Oregon for coming up on 20 years. We pay industry leading wages, paid health insurance for the employees, season end bonuses , often equal to 10% of their yearly gross pay, all expenses paid trips for continuing education &  company retreats for both the employee and the spouse on a yearly basis.  With all that being said, this state has still taken a business from a 40% profit range to a 25% profit range in The last 5 years through increases in taxes and regulations.  With this latest proposal of "free healcare", the tax increases will take my business point of insolvency.  If this becomes law, and it will if Kotek gets back in office, I predict Oregon will plunder headlong into a serious depression. Eclipsing COVID by multiples. The sucking sound, as they say, will be heard across the Western States.  I sincerely hope there's enough young, conservative, willing souls to fight this to the bitter end.  It took them 57 years to finally run me out of the state that I love, but I'm out..
